# Todas as medalhas olímpicas da natação brasileira

Com a notícia de que os Jogos Olímpicos de Tóquio seriam transferidos para o ano de 2021, devido a pandemia do COVID-19, a **SWIM CHANNEL** se concentrou em produção específica sobre o megaevento para que a "chama olímpica" continuasse acesa no coração dos amantes da natação.

Assim nasceu a série: *Todas as medalhas olímpicas da natação brasileira*. As entrevistas acontecem ao vivo pela rede social Instagram ([@swimchannel](https://instagram.com/swimchannel)), tendo iniciado no dia 6 de abril com o maior nadador medalhista olímpico do nosso pais: Gustavo Borges. Desde então todas as segundas e quintas-feiras as 11h, são realizadas entrevistas com extremos detalhes das conquistas brasileiras. Confira o cronograma:

#### Colunistas do UOL

[https://swimchannel.blogosfera.uol.com.br/2020/04/21/todas-as-medalhas-olimpicas-da-natacao-brasileira/](https://swimchannel.blogosfera.uol.com.br/2020/04/21/todas-as-medalhas-olimpicas-da-natacao-brasileira/)

![](https://swimchannel.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/622_1207c030-9757-33ae-8431-9280c767799f.jpg)

Gustavo Borges – Foto: Reprodução

**Episódio 01, dia 06/04: Gustavo Borges e a medalha de prata nos 200m livre de Atlanta-1996**

Sabemos que os 100m livre são a especialidade de Gustavo, porém, o episódio 01 visava escutar do próprio atleta como ele encarava os 200m livre. Na entrevista, tivemos a oportunidade de analisar o ranking mundial dos 200m livre em 1996, quem eram os adversários, as chances de lutar por um lugar ao pódio, a estratégia de prova e a consagração de um veterano.

![](https://swimchannel.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/4x200.png)

O revezamento 4x200m livre medalhista em Moscou-1980 – Foto: Reprodução

**Episódio 02, dia 09/04: Djan Madruga e a medalha de bronze no 4x200m livre em Moscou-1980**

# Relembre a única medalha de ouro da história da natação brasileira nos Jogos

Ao longo de todas as edições dos **[Jogos Olímpicos](https://www.lance.com.br/jogos-de-paris)**, o Brasil conquistou 15 medalhas na Natação. No entanto, apenas uma de ouro. A vitória histórica aconteceu em Pequim-2008, quando Cesar Cielo subiu ao lugar mais alto do pódio na prova dos 50m livre.

# Natação

Na história dos Jogos Olímpicos, a modalidade está presente desde a primeira edição da era moderna, em Atenas 1896. Naquela época, as provas foram disputadas em um ambiente natural, na Baía de Zea. Só nos jogos de 1908, em Londres, é que a natação passou a ser realizada em piscinas.

No começo, as provas eram disputadas apenas por homens. As mulheres entraram no programa olímpico nos jogos de 1912, em Estocolmo.

Explosão física, resistência, força e técnica são qualidades essenciais aos nadadores. Eles quebram barreiras na luta contra o tempo nesse esporte que é, sem dúvidas, um dos grandes atrativos dos Jogos Olímpicos.

Nas provas olímpicas, a piscina tem 50 metros de comprimento. A modalidade é dividida por estilos de nado. São quatro: peito, costas, borboleta e livre. Existem as provas individuais e os revezamentos.

O Brasil participou pela primeira vez da natação nos Jogos Olímpicos Antuérpia 1920, com Orlando Amêndola e Ângelo Gammaro. Em Los Angeles 1932, Maria Lenk fez história ao se tornar a primeira brasileira e sul-americana a nadar nos Jogos Olímpicos.

Até a edição Paris 2024, a modalidade já garantiu 15 medalhas olímpicas ao Brasil. A primeira foi conquistada com Tetsuo Okamoto, bronze nos 1500m livre em Helsinque 1952. O único ouro brasileiro até aqui foi com Cesar Cielo Filho, nos 50m livre de Pequim 2008.

The men's [100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_metre_freestyle "100 metre freestyle") event at the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") took place on 28 July at the [Piscines Bernat Picornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piscines_Bernat_Picornell "Piscines Bernat Picornell") in [Barcelona, Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona,_Spain "Barcelona, Spain").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_100_metre_freestyle#cite_note-SR-1) There were 75 competitors from 52 nations.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_100_metre_freestyle#cite_note-Olympedia-2) Nations had been limited to two swimmers each since the 1984 Games. The event was won by [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)") of the Unified Team. [Gustavo Borges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Borges "Gustavo Borges")'s silver was [Brazil's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Olympic_Committee "Brazilian Olympic Committee") first medal in the men's 100 metre freestyle since 1960. [Stéphan Caron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stéphan_Caron "Stéphan Caron") of France repeated as bronze medalist, the eighth man to win multiple medals in the event. It was the first time since 1968 that the United States had competed and not won the event and the first time since 1956 that the Americans had competed and not taken any medal, as [Jon Olsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Olsen "Jon Olsen") finished fourth and defending champion [Matt Biondi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Biondi "Matt Biondi") came in fifth.

## Background

This was the 21st appearance of the men's 100 metre freestyle. The event has been held at every Summer Olympics except 1900 (when the shortest freestyle was the 200 metres), though the 1904 version was measured in yards rather than metres.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_100_metre_freestyle#cite_note-Olympedia-2)

Five of the eight finalists from the 1988 Games returned: gold medalist [Matt Biondi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Biondi "Matt Biondi") of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Olympic_&_Paralympic_Committee "United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee"), bronze medalist [Stéphan Caron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stéphan_Caron "Stéphan Caron") of France, fourth-place finisher [Gennadiy Prigoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gennadiy_Prigoda "Gennadiy Prigoda") of the Soviet Union (now competing for the Unified Team), sixth-place finisher [Andrew Baildon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Baildon "Andrew Baildon") of Australia, and eighth-place finisher [Tommy Werner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Werner "Tommy Werner") of Sweden.

Biondi was the favorite, having also won the 1991 World Championship and his 1988 world record still standing. Caron and 1991 European Champion [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)") were also contenders.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_100_metre_freestyle#cite_note-Olympedia-2)

Albania, Lithuania, the Maldives, Saudi Arabia, and the Seychelles each made their debut in the event; some former Soviet republics competed as the Unified Team and competitors from Yugoslavia competed as Independent Olympic Participants. The United States made its 20th appearance, most of any nation, having missed only the boycotted 1980 Games.

## Competition format

This [freestyle swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freestyle_swimming "Freestyle swimming") competition used the A/B final format instituted in 1984. The competition consisted of two rounds: heats and finals. The swimmers with the best 8 times in the semifinals advanced to the A final, competing for medals through 8th place. The swimmers with the next 8 times in the semifinals competed in the B final for 9th through 16th place. Swim-offs were used as necessary to determine advancement.

#### Final A

Popov won, well ahead of everyone else. An equipment error resulted in the scoreboard initially displaying Caron as the second-place swimmer and Borges as last. Borges last was an obvious mistake to anyone watching; he had been fighting for second. His touchpad had malfunctioned. Officials reviewed film of "his" finish, assigning him a time of 49.53—equal to Biondi; they then realized that the film had been *of Biondi*. Looking at the correct finish, the officials gave Borges a time of 49.43, good for the silver medal.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_100_metre_freestyle#cite_note-Olympedia-2)
